Parameter stores

Source: R/params.R
zl_params.Rd

A parameter store holds named tensors of up to four dimensions. Its memory belongs to the 'ggml' library, outside R's heap, and is freed when the store is garbage collected. Stores cannot be saved with saveRDS(): a restored store is invalid (zulm_stale_error); use zl_save() and zl_load().

Usage

zl_params()

zl_param(
  p,
  name,
  dim,
  init = zl_init_normal(sd = 0.02),
  type = c("f32", "f16", "bf16")
)

zl_param_get(p, name)

zl_param_set(p, name, value)

zl_param_names(p, types = FALSE)

zl_param_count(p)

zl_param_tensor(p, name)

Arguments

p

A parameter store from zl_params() or zl_load().

name

The parameter's name: a string of 1 to 63 bytes, unique in the store.

dim

Its dimensions: one to four positive whole numbers.

init

How to fill it: see zl_init_normal().

type

The storage type: "f32", "f16" or "bf16".

value

An array of dim(value) equal to the parameter's dimensions, or a vector of the right length for a one-dimensional parameter. NA is refused.

types

For zl_param_names(): TRUE returns the parameters' storage types, named by parameter.

Value

zl_params() returns an empty store. zl_param() and zl_param_set() return the store invisibly. zl_param_get() returns a double vector or array; zl_param_names() the names in the order added; zl_param_count() the total number of values; zl_param_tensor() a handle for use when building a graph, for a parameter or a state tensor (zl_state()).

Details

zl_param() adds a parameter. Its values are stored as type: "f32" (single precision, the default), or "f16" and "bf16" (half precision, for weights that are only read). R doubles are rounded to the nearest representable value; values beyond the type's range become infinite with a zulm_range_warning.

Half precision costs more than storage: 'ggml' converts the activations to the weight's type before a product, so zl_crossprod() with an f16 weight differs from the f32 product by about 1e-3 of the output's scale, and with a bf16 weight by about 2e-3 to 3e-3. Results that must match a reference closely need f32 weights.

An R array of dim = c(d1, d2, d3, d4) is stored with the first index fastest, as R stores it, so values move without reordering.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "w", c(3, 2))
zl_param(p, "b", 2, init = zl_init_zeros())
zl_param_names(p)
#> [1] "w" "b"
zl_param_count(p)
#> [1] 8
zl_param_set(p, "b", c(0.5, -0.5))
zl_param_get(p, "b")
#> [1]  0.5 -0.5
